taxonomyNote: NatureServe moved this species from Mustela to Neogale (Patterson et al. 2021); ADW still uses Mustela frenata.
fieldMarks: Long slender body, small narrow head, long whiskers, short legs
Cinnamon-brown above, white underparts with a yellow tinge
Long bushy tail about 50% of body length
Body 330-420 mm in males, 280-350 mm in females; northern animals turn white in winter, southern ones stay brown
behavior: Primarily nocturnal but frequently seen by day
Eats mainly small mammals, occasionally birds, other small vertebrates and insects
Dens in abandoned burrows, rock crevices, brush piles, stump hollows or among tree roots
Molts in spring and fall, timed by day length
habitat: A wide variety of habitats, usually near water: brushland, open woodland, field edges, riparian grassland, swamps and marshes; not desert or thick forest.
range: Southern Canada, nearly all of the contiguous US (excluding the southwestern deserts), south to Venezuela and Bolivia.

lookalikes.name: Least weasel
lookalikes.howToTell: Far smaller with a short tail and no black tip in winter.
